name: Anjana
body:
Anjana CR 2

This dainty sprite is dressed in a flowing belted tunic, with skin and cloth each so pale as to seem almost translucent, faintly glowing and with long blonde hair adorned with a crown of flowers. She has two transparent wings and carries a small hazel stick and a small bottle at her belt.

XP 600
NG Small fey
Init +3; Senses low-light vision; Perception +8

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 14, flat-footed 11 (+3 Dex, +1 size)
hp 18 (4d6+4)
Fort +2, Ref +7, Will +5; +2 vs. charm and fear DR 5/cold iron; Resist cold 5, electricity 5

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 50 ft. (good)
Ranged jarring jolt +6 (2d8 electricity)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 4th; concentration +6)

At will—guidance
3/day—entangle (DC 13), speak with animals
1/day—gust of wind (DC 14), spike growth (DC 15)

STATISTICS

Str 8, Dex 17, Con 13, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 15
Base Atk +2; CMB +0; CMD 13
Feats Combat Casting, Skill Focus (Perform [sing])
Skills Acrobatics +10, Diplomacy +9, Fly +16, Perception +8, Perform (sing) +12, Stealth +14
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan
SQ healing nectar

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Healing Nectar (Su)

An anjana drinks from her flask or feeds it to an adjacent creature as a standard action. The drinker heals 2d8+4 hit points.

Jarring Jolt (Su)

The jarring jolt has a range of 60 feet. A creature struck by jarring jolt must succeed at a DC 14 Will save or become stunned for 1 round. The save DC is Charisma-based.

These fey can often be mistaken for a sprite. Standing about three feet in height, their forms are very elven in appearance.

Their clothing always includes a belt of some kind to hold the two objects always in an anjana’s possession: her flask of healing nectar and her wand.

An anjana’s flask can vary in appearance, from fine crystal to simple pottery, but always contains nectar gathered from local flowers and instilled with fey magic to provide healing when drunk. The wand acts as a focus for their magic and can deliver nasty jolts to hostile creatures.

An anjana may make her lair near a river, claiming that waterway as her own and devoting herself to its protection.

A river may have more than one anjana as its designated protector, and such anjana will certainly cooperate to mitigate any threat to the waterway. Legends say they dwell in small caves covered in gold near their chosen river, and from this gilded lair she helps those who get lost in her riverine forest and punishes those who damage it.

An anjana’s songs brighten the day if they are happy and darken it if they are sad. Her voice is soft and sweet and her mood contagious to those who listen to it. They often watch over near herding societies, leaving their refuges when the cattle and sheep go up to the mountains, and returning in the autumn when they return to the valleys.

Anjana are often found in forests, and typically friendly to those that respect their homes. They often aid lost travelers to find their way. Those that despoil or threaten the forest home of an anjana will be suitably punished by any and all anjana that make their homes there.

Anjanas often leave some of the silver from their crowns among the bushes where they roam, to make the happiness and fortune of the person who finds them. Their peculiarities vary according to the place, there are areas where it is said that they wear spikes of silver around their waists and on their heads, and bells that give off pearls when they ring.
